conviction_note: Q4 revenue is set by the July guide ($330.5-331.5M FY less $239.4M for 9M = $91.1-92.1M against a $91.4M consensus) and the Q4 tariff refund is already in the margin guide and the EPS bar, so the print turns on the first FY27 guide against a $389M / +17.8% consensus. Weak traffic (Q3 -5.1%, Q4 implied comps -3 to -4%) and tariffs that persist under Section 301 point down; management's stated margin path, Q1 FY27 IP and rewards catalysts, lowered price targets and a 25%-of-float short point up. Net is a near-balanced lean (p_up 52) on a large move scale (12.5%, the name's own 11.9% median, with six of seven prints above 11%). impact_sum (+1.3) and the scaled number (+0.5) agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because p_up holds the uncertainty about the guide.
bar: Q4 FY26 (Jun-Aug) revenue $91.4M. Earnings Whispers ($91.43M, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/KRUS) and Benzinga ($91.4M, updated 2026-10-23) agree, and it sits inside the company's implied Q4 of $91.1-92.1M: FY26 guide $330.5-331.5M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001772177/000119312526297503/krus-ex99_1.htm, 2026-07-07) less 9M sales of $73.5M + $80.0M + $85.9M = $239.4M (Q1 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1772177/000119312526006345/krus-ex99_1.htm, Q2 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1772177/000119312526145572/krus-ex99_1.htm). Q4 EPS consensus $0.17-0.21 depending on source (Benzinga pages $0.17 and $0.20, Earnings Whispers $0.21); year-ago Q4 was $0.20 on $79.4M. FY27 consensus revenue $388.96M (+17.8%) and EPS $0.24, 9 analysts (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/krus/forecast/, updated 2026-10-26). The company gives no comp guide; Craig-Hallum's -3% to -4% implied Q4 comp came from the July call and management did not confirm it.
positioning_check: Short interest 1.72M shares = 24.64% of float (float 6.97M), down from 1.81M the month before; days to cover 6.58 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/krus/statistics/, page updated 2026-11-05) or 9.79 (https://fintel.io/s/us/krus); the sweep had 1.8M / 6.6 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement. Crowded short, covering slightly. No listed options, so there is no skew and no implied move; the baseline uses the 11.87% median reaction. Tape: spot $36.47, 54% below the 52-week high, 18% above the low (about $29.7-30.9 in late October), -8.7% over 20 days and +4.4% over 5 days (it bounced off about $31.80 on 10-27 and $32.65 on 10-29). Price targets cut into the print: Citi $59 to $36 (Neutral) on 2026-10-26, D.A. Davidson $70 to $55 (Buy) on 2026-10-15.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 revenue is effectively pre-announced. The July guide ($330.5-331.5M) less 9M sales of $239.4M implies $91.1-92.1M (+14.7-16.0% on Q4 FY25's $79.4M). The $91.4M consensus sits inside that range. The location count also points to delivery: 91 restaurants at 2026-05-31, 94 by 2026-07-07, and the company's 2026-10-15 notice says 96. So the 16th FY26 unit opened despite the fire-inspection delays, and one FY27 unit is already open.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 (2026-07-07), revenue of $85.9M missed about $86.3-86.5M and EPS beat; the stock fell 8.5% after hours but closed the window +0.79%. Finviz notes three revenue misses in two years.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the company guided the number. It is filed so the panel can see the revenue line is not where the move comes from. A 96-unit count would only add something if the market still doubted the 16-unit FY26 target.
findings.independence: The 96-location count comes from a different document, the company's 2026-10-15 results-date notice (https://finviz.com/news/403295/kura-sushi-usa-to-announce-fiscal-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results-on-november-5-2026). The Q1 and Q2 sales come from separate 8-Ks.

findings.finding: On the July call management said Q4 would include a one-time refund of tariffs paid 'for our other cost items', and raised the FY26 restaurant-level margin guide to about 18.5% with that refund inside it. Courts ordered IEEPA duties refunded to all importers of record with interest (March 2026), and CBP opened a refund process on 2026-04-20. So the refund is real, but its size is undisclosed, and it covers non-food items because food is likely imported by others.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior refund on this name. On other names in this repo, tariff refunds landing in the quarter split by the direction of guidance: two rose double digits and two fell double digits.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is inside the 18.5% margin guide and the $0.20 EPS bar. The only unpriced part is the size. If the refund also covered food-ingredient duties paid as importer of record, it could be several million dollars against Q4 net income of about $2.4M (12.2M shares x $0.20). The market would then be anchoring EPS above $0.25, and it is not.
findings.independence: The legal mechanism is independent of the company: https://taxprofblog.aals.org/2026/04/21/ieepa-tariff-refund-process-begins/. The company-level size is unsourced.

findings.finding: Tariff relief for FY27 is limited. The Supreme Court ended IEEPA duties in February 2026, but a Section 122 global tariff ran 2026-02-24 to 2026-07-24, and Section 301 duties with a 12.5% floor on goods of Japan replaced it the same minute. Kura's imported ingredients therefore still carry about 12.5% against 15% under IEEPA, not zero. Separately, Asian fishing-fleet fuel costs more than doubled after the Strait of Hormuz closed in April 2026. Both bear on the FY27 COGS line, which management expected to run about 30% of sales in FY26 (+200bp from tariffs).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The tariff-driven COGS rise was named in the Q1 FY26 print (2026-01-07, stock +16.7% anyway on comps and traffic) and the Q2 print (2026-04-07, -17.8% on the CFO exit and Hormuz fish-fuel costs).
findings.why_not_priced: The tariff regime is public. What is unpriced is how much of a 'tariff relief' margin story survives in the FY27 guide. Management said it aims for a 20% margin 'regardless of tariff relief', so a guide that assumes relief would surprise on the upside and one that assumes the 12.5% floor would not. This is macro-to-company transmission and the company has not confirmed it.
findings.independence: Hormuz fish-fuel costs: https://www.tridge.com/news/kura-sushi-usas-17-nasdaq-slide-shows-toughe-awxcvjgq (2026-04-09). Section 122 expiry: https://borderbuddy.com/trade-tariff-news/section-122-is-out-section-301-is-in. Shares the COGS line with the margin finding below, which points the other way and rests on a different statement.

findings.finding: Traffic is the weak line going into the first FY27 guide. Q3 comps were -0.4%, made of traffic -5.1% and price/mix +4.7%. Craig-Hallum's -3% to -4% implied Q4 comp was not confirmed by management, which promised only 'slightly positive comps for the full year' (9M comps +1.8%). Management also said FY27 pricing will be below FY26's 4%+, so FY27 comps need traffic to recover. Placer.ai's Q3 2026 casual-dining data show visits flat (+0.2%) overall and -2.3% in trade areas below $81K household income (about 45% of visits).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Comp/traffic has been the line this name trades on. In Q1 FY26 (Jan 2026) comps were -2.5%, but traffic improving into Dec-Jan bought +16.7%. The Q2 FY26 +8.6% comp was sold (-17.8%, with the CFO exit). The last FY-guide print, Nov 2025 (Q4 FY25 comp +0.2%), fell 11.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is 54% off its high and targets were cut in October. What is not priced is a soft comp assumption in the FY27 revenue guide. Consensus at $389M (+17.8%) needs about 20% unit growth with roughly flat comps. If the market had already priced negative FY27 comps, consensus would sit nearer $375-380M.
findings.independence: The industry proxy is Placer.ai, 2026-10-26: https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/four-recipes-for-casual-dining-growth-in-q3-2026. The Q4 comp estimate and management's comp language come from the transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1881185-20260708), a different document from the release.

findings.finding: A crowded short into the print: 1.72M shares short = 24.6% of a 6.97M float, 6.6-9.8 days to cover, a slight decline from 1.81M. The stock is near its 52-week low and has bounced 4.4% in five days, and no options market exists to hedge with.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +31.6% move in April 2025 and +16.7% in January 2026 show how far this float moves on an acceptable print. In this repo, two shorts into names with 18% and 23% of float short squeezed more than 20%.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public. The squeeze is a mechanism that pays only if the guide is merely in line. With 25% of float short and about seven days to cover, a non-negative guide forces buying over the exit session that the pre-print price cannot hold.
findings.independence: Fintel (24.64%, DTC 9.79): https://fintel.io/s/us/krus. The sweep row cites curvedtrading at 2026-09-30 (1.8M, 6.6 days) and Benzinga at 26.8%.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 catalysts are already in motion and management will be able to cite them on the call. The upgraded rewards app (three tiers, Yellowfin/Bigeye/Bluefin) went out on schedule around 2026-10-06. A nationwide Persona IP ran from 2026-08-01, and the Nintendo 'Yoshi' campaign is set for Nov-Dec; management sized marquee IPs like Kirby and Yoshi at a mid-single-digit comp contribution, against low single digits for base IPs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Jan 2026 the Kirby IP ran Dec-Jan and management reported improving December/January traffic; the stock rose 16.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are announced programmes, so their existence is priced. What is not priced is any Q1-to-date traffic number they produce: Sept/Oct traffic is unknown, and the market has given IP-driven traffic no credit at a 54% drawdown.
findings.independence: Rewards relaunch: https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/kura-sushi-usa-aktie-neues-treueprogramm-belohnt-stammgaste-mit-mehr-punkten (date 2026-10-06 per search snippet, not checked on the URL path). Persona: https://segabits.com/blog/2026/07/30/atlus-and-kura-sushi-usa-bring-persona-to-restaurants-nationwide-august-1/ (2026-07-30).

findings.finding: There has been no permanent CFO since 2026-04-28. CEO Hajime Uba is interim CFO and has also taken on COO duties. EDGAR shows no 8-K since the 2026-07-07 results (only a Form 144 and 13G/As), so no CFO had been appointed by the print, and the FY27 guide will be the first set without a CFO.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The April 2026 CFO departure coincided with a -17.8% reaction to a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The vacancy is known. If a CFO appointment came with the release it would be a small positive; a guide without one keeps a credibility discount. The sign depends on what is announced.

findings.finding: Management's stated margin path supports the FY27 EPS guide. Q3 restaurant-level margin was 19.1% (up from 18.2%) and labor 30.6% (down 250bp) on the reservation system and staffing. The FY26 margin guide was raised to about 18.5%. Management said it would approach the 20% target 'a lot faster than we would have expected', with robotic dishwashers rolling out in FY27, and expects G&A to leverage. FY27 consensus EPS is only $0.24.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin beats have not reliably been bought. Q3 FY26 (margin up 90bp, EPS beat) closed +0.79%, and Q2 FY26 (EPS beat) fell 17.8% on other news.
findings.why_not_priced: A FY27 margin guide of 19-20% on about $389M of revenue implies EPS well above $0.24 once G&A leverages from 12% of sales. Consensus at $0.24 suggests the street does not believe the path, or has priced tariff and fish-cost headwinds against it.
findings.independence: The Q3 margin and labor numbers are in the 8-K release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001772177/000119312526297503/krus-ex99_1.htm), a primary document. The forward claim is the same transcript as the IP finding. The tariff-regime finding above weighs against it on the COGS line.

findings.finding: The sell-side cut targets in the three weeks before the print: Citi $59 to $36 (Neutral, 2026-10-26) and D.A. Davidson $70 to $55 (Buy, 2026-10-15). Consensus FY27 revenue had drifted from $410.8M earlier in the year to $389M, so the bar the FY27 guide meets has already been lowered.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior: the target cuts after the July print were followed by a slide from about $46 (Aug 1) to about $31 (late Oct).
findings.why_not_priced: A Citi target at the spot price says the street is not positioned for upside. The ambiguity: the cut may reflect a negative Q1 traffic read the market already holds, which would make it priced, not a lowered bar.
findings.independence: Fintel lists the same Oct 15 and Oct 26 actions: https://fintel.io/s/us/krus. The older FY27 estimate path is in https://www.newsquantified.com/krus/stock-report/kura-sushi-usa-class-a-q1-2026-everything-you-need-0fgn3d.

searched_and_found_nothing: Q4 FY26 results or any pre-announcement: none found before the print (EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-07-07)
Placer.ai chain-level 2026 visit data for Kura Revolving Sushi Bar: the free tool shows no 2026 series
Black Box Intelligence monthly comps for Jun-Sep 2026: no 2026 figures found
Parent Kura Sushi Inc (TSE 2695) disclosures on the US subsidiary since July: none found; the parent's FY Oct-2026 forecast is unchanged on Yahoo Japan
Litigation: a $0.9M wage-and-hour settlement, already accrued at 2026-05-31, so immaterial
Size of the Q4 tariff refund: not disclosed anywhere I could reach; the 10-Q MD&A and notes could not be fetched past the financial statements
Cause of the mid/late-October slide (-17.5% week to about Oct 23): no company event found beyond the D.A. Davidson and Citi target cuts
Customer complaints or forum signals: not pursued beyond the IP and rewards newsroom items

rejected_candidates.detail: The price level ($64.99) contradicts the sealed spot of $36.47 and the late-October quotes of about $32-35, so this is a prior-year story relabelled with a 2026 date.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Finviz Q4 preview citing EPS -$0.16 and revenue $73.65M
rejected_candidates.detail: This is a prior-quarter preview; the July 8-K guide implies Q4 revenue of $91.1-92.1M.

rejected_candidates.candidate: ChartMill FY26 consensus of $340.86M and Q4 revenue of $95.94M
rejected_candidates.detail: These are pre-guide-cut figures; the company guide ($330.5-331.5M) and two current sources ($91.4M) replace them.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Fintel's 'price target decreased 15.14% to $66.91' and '-17.50% from prior week' items
rejected_candidates.detail: The target drift is folded into the analyst-cut finding; the week's move is already reflected in the sealed tape.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The 20-day run-up of -8.7% and the 54% drawdown already carry the bearish traffic and tariff case, while the 25% short float and the 5-day bounce cut toward upside if the FY27 guide is merely in line; my findings net slightly positive, mildly against the run-up.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (a finding inside the guided range is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): Q4 revenue +0.3 -> +0.1.
Lesson 2 (one-offs below operating income with no path to the guide): tariff refund +0.3 -> +0.2; it is already inside the 18.5% margin guide.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission is filed small): tariff-regime/fish-fuel finding -0.5 -> -0.4.
Lesson 7 (a crowded short shrinks a negative): traffic finding -1.5 -> -1.2, given 24.6% of float short.
Lesson 5 (positioning is not a company fact): short-squeeze finding +1.5 -> +1.2, kept as a filed mechanism per the core.
Lesson 1 (this name has not paid for margin beats): margin-path finding +1.0 -> +0.8.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the analyst-cut finding's ambiguity (the cuts may reflect a priced negative) took it from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, understatement is the systematic error): abs_move_pct kept at 12.5, above the 11.87% median, and not shrunk for sign uncertainty.
